title: Swift: Collections
description: Write a Swift program demonstrating arrays, dictionaries, sets, and functional operations.

codeTemplate.swift:
// Array
var numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
print("Original: \(numbers)")
numbers.append(6)
print("After append: \(numbers)")
print("Sum: \(numbers.reduce(0, +))")

// Dictionary
var scores = ["Alice": 95, "Bob": 87, "Charlie": 92]
print("\nScores: \(scores)")
print("Alice score: \(scores["Alice"]!)")
scores["Diana"] = 78
print("After add: \(scores)")

// Set
let evenSet: Set = [2, 4, 6, 8, 10]
let smallSet: Set = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
print("\nUnion: \(evenSet.union(smallSet).sorted())")
print("Intersection: \(evenSet.intersection(smallSet).sorted())")

// Functional
let doubled = numbers.map { $0 * 2 }
print("\nDoubled: \(doubled)")
let evens = numbers.filter { $0 % 2 == 0 }
print("Evens: \(evens)")

hints: Arrays are ordered collections, dictionaries are key-value, sets are unordered unique
Dictionaries return Optionals — use `!` to force unwrap when sure
